welcome.title: Welcome to Humidity Intelligence
welcome.description:
Humidity Intelligence is a deterministic Home Assistant control engine for humidity, air quality, condensation, mould risk, and carbon monoxide safety. It uses configured sensors, room mappings, zones, outputs, and runtime gates to make one explainable control decision per cycle.

Recommended setup method

For most homes, start small. Add a few core sensors first, ideally one humidity sensor and one temperature sensor for a main room. Continue through setup and save the integration. You can then return to Options to add more rooms, sensors, zones, air-quality inputs, humidifiers, alerts, and dashboard exports.

This staged method gives you a saved baseline to return to, makes setup easier to validate, and avoids losing a long first-run configuration.

Advanced setup method

If you already know your full sensor layout, you can add all sensors during first setup and configure everything in one pass.

Next, Humidity Intelligence will check optional dashboard add-ons. Backend control does not require these cards, but generated dashboards look best when they are installed.

Full Configuration Walkthrough: {walkthrough_url}

zone_thresholds.title: Zone Thresholds
zone_thresholds.description:
Selected zone triggers use recommended thresholds unless customised.

{advanced_note}

Humidity above house average uses the selected rooms' average humidity compared to the whole-house average. The threshold is the delta in % points.

Condensation risk uses dew-point spread:
spread = temperature - dew_point
Lower spread = higher risk (air is closer to saturation).
Interpretation is season-aware and relative to the active target profile. The configured slider remains deterministic and is mapped to a seasonal spread threshold.

Mould risk is derived from humidity relative to the active target band plus dew-point spread, normalized to levels:
Level 1 = Watch
Level 2 = Risk
Level 3 = Danger
So a threshold of 2 triggers when risk reaches Risk or Danger for the active profile.

ui_install.title: UI Cards
ui_install.description:
Select the Manual-card layouts to export. The tablet layout is selected by default for initial setup. Later, dump_cards without a layout exports all cached layouts; supply layout to export one layout only.

V1 Mobile remains available in this candidate but is deprecated for new dashboards. Use V2 Mobile for new dashboards. Removing V1 Mobile requires a separate approved migration.

HI writes card fragments under /config/humidity_intelligence/ui/ and posts a notification with every exact path created during setup. It does not create, register, replace, or delete Home Assistant dashboards. Multi-entry installations add an entry-qualified token to the filename.

Updating from an older HI release: a file such as /config/humidity_intelligence_cards_v2_mobile.yaml is a retained legacy root file and is no longer refreshed. Do not copy that old root file after upgrading. Use only the exact /config/humidity_intelligence/ui/... path in the new notification. If File Editor was already open, refresh its file tree after export.

Configured alerts:
{configured_alerts}

Warning: The backend logic will work without frontend dependencies, but the UI cards may render incorrectly unless the required custom cards are installed (card-mod, button-card, mod-card, apexcharts-card).

To load a card: open the exact /config/humidity_intelligence/ui/... path from the notification in File Editor → copy the complete YAML → create or open a Home Assistant dashboard → Edit dashboard → Add card → Manual → paste YAML. The export is a card fragment; do not copy it to /config/dashboards/.

Next step: Configuration Walkthrough: {walkthrough_url}

options_output_observation.title: Output monitoring
options_output_observation.description: Optional monitoring only. These settings never change output commands. Changes stay in this session: choose Keep changes and return, then choose Save changes on the main settings page to apply them. Discard removes monitoring edits made since you last kept changes and returned to the main settings; earlier kept changes remain in the session.

options_output_settings.title: Monitoring and dashboard view
options_output_settings.description: Monitoring is optional. Native presentation keeps the existing Outputs panel. Adaptive presentation needs the packaged dashboard resource and a fresh card export. Turning monitoring off never changes device control. These changes are not saved until you choose Save changes on the main settings page.

options_output_binding.title: Monitoring rule
options_output_binding.description: Choose an output already configured in HI, the reading to monitor, and what that reading means. A reading from a shared device does not identify which output has a fault. Review the selected entities and exact rule on the next page, including the current identity when replacing an entity.

options_output_rule.title: When should HI show a notice?
options_output_rule.description: For a value rule, enter exact case-sensitive values for attention and clear. The two lists must not overlap; any other value remains unknown. For a number rule, choose the threshold using your device guidance. Comparisons are strict: a value equal to the threshold does not trigger the notice. This rule does not bind or convert units.

data.active_values: Show the notice for these values
data.clear_values: Clear the notice for these values

options_output_manage.title: Manage monitoring rules
options_output_manage.description: Rules with missing or changed sources stay saved until you change them. Pausing keeps the reading as context and preserves its saved rule; monitoring coverage stays incomplete. Resume uses the saved rule, or standard automatic discovery if none is saved. Removing a custom rule does not suppress a standard automatic meaning.

options_output_import.title: Import experimental companion rules
options_output_import.description: Choose a companion explicitly bound to this HI entry. Only matching current identities are eligible. The preview never modifies the companion. Historical pending observation custody is not imported: the integrated observer starts from the current Home Assistant snapshot. Disable the companion separately after validating a migration.

options_output_confirm.title: Review monitoring change
options_output_confirm.description:
{preview}

Review the selected entities and exact rule. Confirming keeps this change in the current session; it does not save it. Choose Keep changes and return, then choose Save changes on the main settings page to apply them. Leave the box unchecked to discard only this proposed change.

options_output_observation_error.title: Saved monitoring settings need review

house_humidity_mean_7d_missing.title: House humidity drift needs a Statistics helper
house_humidity_mean_7d_missing.description: Humidity Intelligence cannot calculate 7-day house humidity drift until `{dependency_entity}` exists. Create a Home Assistant Statistics helper named House Humidity Mean 7d using `{source_entity}` as the source, state characteristic `mean`, and max age 7 days. The helper entity ID must be exactly `sensor.house_humidity_mean_7d`; rename the entity ID manually if Home Assistant creates a different one. Drift will stay unavailable until Home Assistant reports sufficient recorder/statistics coverage. Do not fabricate history.
